data.body:
PHASE 2 BLOCKED ON A DISPROOF OF THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY (rebar-debug; no code written for this
ticket). The root cause in the description is CONFIRMED and I am not disputing it. What I could
not do is implement the fix it prescribes, because the mechanism it names cannot produce a cache
READ at either site — so it would convert both calls from full price to full price + the 1.25x
write premium. Detail below so this can be re-scoped rather than re-investigated.

## The mechanism-level disproof (not an estimate — read off pydantic-ai)

Both options the description weighs place the breakpoint AFTER the entire message list:

* `anthropic_cache_messages` -> `_apply_message_cache_control`
  (.venv/.../pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py:1770-1795): "Apply per-block `cache_control` to the
  last content block of the LAST MESSAGE."
* `anthropic_cache` (automatic top-level) -> `_build_automatic_cache_control` (ibid. 1719-1736);
  Anthropic's own docs describe it as auto-caching the last cacheable block. On Bedrock/Vertex it
  degrades to `_apply_per_block_caching_fallback`, which calls the SAME
  `_apply_message_cache_control`.

So under either option the marked span ENDS with the per-call-unique tail:

* coach_notes: `resolve_prompt_cached` builds `instructions = volatile + base_instructions`
  (prompting/prompts.py:438-476). volatile is `# Plan under review` + `{{plan}}`; base_instructions
  is that run's SURVIVING FINDINGS list (plan-review.yaml:252-254). The findings differ every run,
  so the marked span is unique every run.
* enrich/ticket-digest: `instructions=source` is one ticket's text (enrich.py:96-105) — unique by
  construction, as the description already says.

A cache entry whose span always ends in unique bytes is WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. It can never
be read, on either site. The guard the description asks for would therefore have to exclude BOTH
sites, which makes the change inert rather than merely narrow.

## Why coach_notes cannot recover its cost this way even in principle

The description's premise is that the coach's plan is "ALREADY in the cache, written by the Pass-1
finders". That entry is keyed on the finders' full request prefix (render order tools -> system ->
messages), whose SYSTEM block is `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body`
(plan_review/passes.py:282,290). The coach's system block is its own 9-line stance prose. The two
requests therefore diverge at the first system byte, so no coach request — in ANY message slot —
can read the finders' entry.

Also relevant to the economics: coach_notes is a single step behind `branch: coach_gate`
(plan-review.yaml:243-254), not inside a `loop`/`map`/`batch`. It is exactly ONE call per gate run.
There is no second coach call within the 5-minute TTL to read whatever the first wrote.

## What WOULD work (proposed re-scope, not implemented)

A read requires a breakpoint placed BEFORE the volatile tail, at bytes shared with another request
in the same run. Two pieces, both larger than this ticket's stated scope:

1. `pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint` (messages.py:692; honoured at anthropic.py:1234) is the only
   mechanism that can put a breakpoint MID-message — i.e. between the reusable plan and the
   per-run findings. That is a RunRequest content-list change, which the description explicitly
   notes today's design avoids so the structured-output retry path stays untouched.
2. Even with the CachePoint, the coach needs a REUSABLE counterpart. The saving only materialises
   if the plan-bearing span is a byte-identical prefix shared with the Pass-1 finder requests and
   a breakpoint sits at that shared boundary. That is a plan-review-wide shared-prefix redesign
   (passes.py / pass1.py), not a `cache_settings_for` change.

## What DID land, on the sibling ticket

AC4 of this ticket ("`warn_if_cache_ineffective` measures the MARKED PREFIX rather than total
`input_tokens`, so the warning names the cause; a test covers a large-total / small-marked-prefix
call") is IMPLEMENTED under e3cd-ba36-41c3-4661, since it is that ticket's core change and landing
it twice would have put two mechanisms at one seam. The new warning reports the coach_notes shape
(150-token marked prefix, ~6928 unmarked) naming the marked prefix and the model's floor, covered
by tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py::
test_large_total_with_tiny_marked_prefix_warns_and_names_the_marked_prefix.

AC1/AC2/AC3 are NOT met and should be re-written against the CachePoint + shared-prefix design
above before anyone picks this up again. AC5 is operator-attested and unaffected.
